question: Did the canonical orientation fix change any computed value at primes where the plain square-root branch was already self-dual-surviving?
answer: No. Zero value differences across the three cells compared.
why_route_differs: One row cache was rebuilt by the merge, so those rows were recomputed rather than served from cache, and one derivative row reached its value through the dense-I plan in one run and from cache in the other. output_hash matches in every case.
why_it_holds: orientation_normalised_L tries the plain branch first and keeps it when the self-dual space survives. At 32749, 32719, 32717, 32713 and 32693 it does, so the frame L is bit-identical to the pre-fix frame and every downstream value follows. Only 32707 and 32771, where the plain branch fails, get a different -- and correct -- frame.
consequence: The pre-fix cell VALUES were mathematically correct. They are superseded as publication certificates because the evaluator provenance changed, not because the arithmetic was wrong.
